interpretation: None of the 3 smoke records complete inside decode_timeout_seconds=30 after the lexer/scanner cache fix. Two of three (hero, callout) reproduce the identical fallback_output outcome and near-identical ~30.0-30.1s wall time as the pre-fix baseline, with meaningful_program_rate unchanged (0.0 / 1.0 respectively) and compiler_ms still ~97% of total wall time. The fix is real and independently confirmed here: per-call compiler_ms/build_completion_forest cost dropped 5.6x (hero) and 8.3x (callout) -- larger than the fix's own ~2-2.1x isolated micro-benchmark -- but the decode loop simply performs proportionally more forward/prefill calls within the same fixed wall budget (hero 3->17 calls, callout 4->33 calls) instead of finishing sooner, so total wall time stays pinned at the 30s ceiling either way. This is the second independent finding to confirm proposed_fix_sketch item 1 from decode-compiler-tree-deadline-swallow-finding.md (the deadline-swallow / missing check_decode_deadline() calls in the compiler-tree per-position loop) is still the operative blocker for hero and callout, exactly as #1173's own 'Next steps' predicted.
side_observation_not_claimed: smoke_button_01's decode_outcome classification shifted from fallback_output (pre-fix) to runtime_timeout (post-fix) on an otherwise-identical checkpoint+flags rerun. lever-decode-nondeterminism-hashseed-ruled-out-measured-results.md already established that decode_outcome classification varies run-to-run under real wall-clock scheduling even with everything else pinned (not a seedable RNG effect). This single n=1-rep before/after pair is not sufficient to attribute the shift to the lexer-cache fix specifically -- flagged as an observation, not claimed as caused by the fix.
